scenario: A beginner has been drinking instant coffee and wants to make brewed coffee at home without buying equipment that will be abandoned within a few months. The beginner is comparing a captured six-cup stovetop moka bundle with a ground-coffee sample, separate pre-ground dark- and light-roast bags, and a whole-bean sampler that would require a suitable grinder and brewer. Repeated claims about dark roast having more caffeine, coffee going stale on a fixed schedule, and a moka pot making machine espresso must be checked before choosing a staged starting path. Stove compatibility, desired serving size and strength, cleanup tolerance, current seller and return terms, roast or pack dates, and the total cost of a complete whole-bean system are not yet known.

rules.roast_caffeine_measurement_scope_v1: The frozen caffeine reference gives serving-level examples, states that arabica typically contains about half the caffeine of robusta, and says dark-roast coffee generally has very slightly less caffeine than lighter roast because roasting reduces caffeine content. This rebuts the beginner shortcut that a dark label itself means a larger caffeine dose, but it does not determine the exact caffeine in any captured bag or cup. The illy listing identifies a dark-roast 100 percent arabica ground moka product, while the DOTA listing identifies a light-roast ground arabica product and offers roast variants. Neither listing provides a standardized dose, measured caffeine, grind mass, water ratio, extraction yield, or brewed serving result. A cup comparison therefore requires bean species, dose or mass, grind, method, water ratio, serving size, and an actual caffeine measurement rather than roast color alone.
rules.freshness_grinding_commitment_scope_v1: The storage reference distinguishes roasted whole beans from grounds, recommends airtight light-protected storage for whole beans, and says increased surface area causes grounds to go stale in days rather than weeks. The preparation reference says roasted beans must be ground before brewing, identifies grind size, water temperature, brew time, and coffee-to-water ratio as extraction variables, and notes that whole or ground coffee is often vacuum packed to limit oxidation. The burr-mill reference explains adjustable coarse-to-fine grinding and that grind ranges differ across espresso, pour-over, drip, French press, and other methods. These sources justify treating whole-bean freshness and method-matched grinding as a system decision, not as proof that every whole-bean bag stays fresh for a fixed number of weeks. The Java Planet listing offers a whole-bean sampler but no grinder, brewer, roast date, opened-package storage outcome, or total-system cost, so it cannot by itself support the whole-bean route for this beginner.
rules.moka_product_and_method_scope_v1: The frozen moka reference says a moka pot uses vapor pressure and heat-driven gas expansion to pass hot water through ground coffee. It also states that typical moka extraction uses about one to two bar while espresso standards specify nine bar, so moka coffee is not considered espresso. The captured Puerto Rican bundle listing displays $34.99, 73 percent of 100 from three reviews, SKU B09PHVT7FF, a six-cup aluminum stovetop maker, and a four-ounce ground-coffee sample; it calls the device a stovetop espresso maker and says steam pressure drives water through grounds. The illy listing displays $12.10, 80 percent of 100 from twelve reviews, SKU B08QG21HWB, and says its ground moka coffee is finely ground for a stovetop moka pot. Together these establish a captured compatible product category and a possible low-commitment trial, but they do not independently establish cafe quality, nine-bar espresso, actual cup output, stove compatibility, safety, cleanup burden, durability, or beginner retention.
rules.listing_and_owner_evidence_boundary_v1: The DOTA light-roast ground listing displays $15.99, 87 percent of 100 from twelve reviews, and SKU B08MBKJGCP; the Java Planet whole-bean sampler displays $34.99 with no reviews and SKU B01MSNNM5X. These are frozen offer facts and seller descriptions, not sensory tests or longitudinal beginner outcomes. A French-press discussion contains one author's enthusiasm, cleanup concerns, a report of plunger threading failing after about two months, and a comment that pour-over can require fresh beans and a good grinder; it is useful for identifying maintenance, fragility, and grinder-cost questions but is not a controlled comparison of the captured products. The two short grinder posts are especially limited: one reports eleven years of daily use without naming a verifiable model in the frozen body, and the other reports daily use of a Braun coffee or spice grinder since 1992. They are distractor anecdotes and cannot support a new grinder model, a grinder category lifetime, or a purchase recommendation.
rules.beginner_coffee_system_preflight_v1: Before choosing a path, verify the exact moka maker's stove and material compatibility, nominal versus actual beverage output, serving fit, valve and gasket condition, grind requirement, cleaning and stopping procedure, current seller, return path, and whether the stated sample is included. For any separate pre-ground path, identify the exact compatible brewer and total cost. For the whole-bean path, identify a method-matched grinder, adjustment range, current cost, cleaning and retention burden, warranty, and brewer. Record roast or pack date and storage plan rather than assuming a universal freshness deadline. Use a small quantity and a returnable or already-owned brewer for the first repeated-use trial, track preparation time, cleanup, taste and whether the routine is actually sustained, and only then add a grinder or premium beans.
rules.evidence_bounded_beginner_coffee_decisio: The frozen evidence does not support a unique best coffee or durable equipment winner. The whole-bean sampler plus new grinder is not an admissible immediate recommendation because no exact coffee grinder or complete system cost is captured, and the pre-ground plus separate-brewer path is incomplete because no exact compatible separate brewer is frozen. If the beginner verifies stove and material compatibility, serving output, safety and cleanup, current seller and return terms, the captured moka bundle is the only frozen offer that combines a brewer with a ground-coffee sample and is admissible as a narrow, reversible trial for strong moka coffee. It must not be sold as machine espresso or as proven cafe quality, and the separate illy bag should not be added until the included sample and routine have been tried. If those checks fail or the user does not want moka-style coffee, defer the exact purchase and first verify a complete method-specific system. A grinder, premium whole beans, or larger recurring coffee purchase becomes admissible only after the beginner demonstrates repeated use and supplies the missing exact-product, total-cost, and method-fit evidence.
